statements.impact_statement: CVE-2025-47273 (GHSA-5rjg-fvgr-3xxf): a path traversal in setuptools' PackageIndex.download, in setuptools/package_index.py, lets a crafted URL write files outside the download directory; fixed in setuptools 78.1.1 (https://github.com/pypa/setuptools/security/advisories/GHSA-5rjg-fvgr-3xxf, https://github.com/pypa/setuptools/issues/4946). k8s-sidecar is a Python application installed in a virtual environment with its dependencies. Listed the files of every published k8s-sidecar package for Alpine 3.24 in the DHI Alpine repository, 2.10.1-r0 to the current 2.14.3-r5, x86_64 and aarch64 (40 packages, each checked against the repository index checksum): no build contains the setuptools package, so none contains setuptools/package_index.py or setuptools' PackageIndex class. The setuptools 70.3.0 that scanners report comes from pip's vendor list (pip/_vendor/vendor.txt names setuptools==70.3.0): the builds from 2.10.1-r0 to 2.14.1-r1 include pip (26.1.2 in 2.10.1-r0, 26.2 after), which vendors only the pkg_resources module from that setuptools release (pip/_vendor/pkg_resources), and pkg_resources does not contain PackageIndex. pip's own pip/_internal/models/index.py defines an unrelated PackageIndex class that only holds index URLs and downloads nothing. The builds from 2.14.1-r2 to 2.14.3-r5 do not include pip.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2025-47273 (GHSA-5rjg-fvgr-3xxf) is a path traversal in setuptools' PackageIndex.download that lets a crafted URL write files outside the download directory; setuptools 78.1.1 fixes it (https://github.com/pypa/setuptools/security/advisories/GHSA-5rjg-fvgr-3xxf, https://github.com/pypa/setuptools/issues/4946, https://github.com/pypa/setuptools/commit/250a6d17978f9f6ac3ac887091f2d32886fbbb0b). No published build of this owner contains a vulnerable setuptools. Checked every airflow package published in the DHI Debian repository, 3.3.0-0 to 3.4.0-7 for amd64 and arm64, including the wheels inside them. The builds from 3.3.0-0 to 3.4.0-0 contain no setuptools distribution; babel and cffi ship small setuptools integration modules that import it, and they do nothing without it. The builds from 3.4.0-1 to 3.4.0-7 contain setuptools 84.2.1 in two places: installed in the application's Python environment under /usr/lib/airflow, and as the setuptools wheel that virtualenv embeds for new environments, which is byte-identical to the 84.2.1 wheel on PyPI. 84.2.1 is newer than the fixed 78.1.1, and neither copy contains setuptools/package_index.py, the module that held PackageIndex. The range therefore starts the fixed side at the first published build, 3.3.0-0.
